title: Sicilian heritage in a mostly Irish town
summary: Being Sicilian in Mount Morris and realizing he was Italian only at college, where he met his first black friend, Hal.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: What role did your Italian heritage have in this whole thing? I noticed that you were written about in a new book about jazz musicians and the Italian heritage.

Well you know we were, we were in a town that was mostly Irish American and we were the Sicilians. And we were pretty low on the totem pole. But it wasn’t in your face every day, because our group was pretty much among our ethnic neighbors and family. But you know the Italian thing I never really thought about it until I got into college. I didn’t know I was Italian until I got to college and someone called me a name. You know really, because we never thought about that. Everybody had a name like ours in our town except for the others, the other side. And I’m not being jive about this but I really didn’t think about that race thing because we weren’t raised as, you’ve got to remember my father came from Sicily so the racism was not bare, fundamentally there was nothing there.
